items.readable_text:
Content:
Recall that the double Integral of the function [MATH: f(x,y) = 1] over a domain [MATH: D\subset \mathbb R^2] is simply the area of [MATH: D\mathbin{:}]
[MATH: \textrm{Area}\ \!(D) = \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D} 1 \cdot \textrm d A = \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D} \ \textrm d A]

Content:
We have a similar result for triple integrals:

Content:
> If [MATH: R] is a region in three-dimensional space, then the volume of [MATH: R] is given by
> [MATH: \textrm{Volume}(R) = \iiint\limits_{R} \textrm{d}V.]

Content:
In other words, the volume of [MATH: R] equals the triple integral of the function [MATH: f(x,y,z)=1] over [MATH: R.]

Content:
For example, let's use triple integrals to find the volume of the rectangular prism shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/66f4da5f969fef77ff61a6e063ea48ed]

Content:
Notice that our solid can be written in set-builder notation as

Content:
[MATH: R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 2, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 3 \big\}.]

Content:
Therefore, the volume of [MATH: R] is

Content:
[MATH: V|= ∭_(R)dV; = ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{0}^{2}∫_{0}^{3}dzdydx; = ∫_{0}^{1}dx ⋅ ∫_{0}^{2}dy ⋅ ∫_{0}^{3}dz; = (1 − 0) ⋅ (2 − 0) ⋅ (3 − 0); = 6.]

Content:
Note: We get the same value using the formula for the volume of a rectangular prism:

Content:
[MATH: V|= length ⋅ width ⋅ height; = 1 ⋅ 2 ⋅ 3; = 6]

Content:
Let's see some more examples.

sections.readable_text:
Find the volume of the solid [MATH: R,] given by
[MATH: R = \Big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 1 \leq y \leq 2, \: 0 \leq z \leq \sqrt{2y}, \: 0 \leq x \leq yz \Big\}.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Notice that we have a three-dimensional type II region.

Therefore, the volume of [MATH: R] is given by the following triple integral:

[MATH: V|= ∭_(R)dV; = ∫_{1}^{2}∫_{0}^{sqrt(2y)}∫_{0}^{yz}dxdzdy; = ∫_{1}^{2}∫_{0}^{sqrt(2y)}[x]_{x = 0}^{x = yz}dzdy; = ∫_{1}^{2}∫_{0}^{sqrt(2y)}yzdzdy; = ∫_{1}^{2}y[(z^{2})/(2)]_{z = 0}^{z = sqrt(2y)}dy; = ∫_{1}^{2}(y)/(2)(sqrt(2y))^{2}dy; = ∫_{1}^{2}y^{2}dy; = [(y^{3})/(3)]_{y = 1}^{y = 2}; = (1)/(3)(8 − 1) − 0; = (7)/(3)]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Notice that our solid can be written as the type I region

[MATH: R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (x,y) \in D, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 4-x-y \big\},]

where

[MATH: D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 2 \big\}]

is the projection of [MATH: R] onto the [MATH: xy]-plane, shown below.

Hence, the type I representation of [MATH: R] is

[MATH: R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 2, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 4-x-y \big\}.]

Therefore, the volume of [MATH: R] is given by the following triple integral:

[MATH: V|= ∭_(R)dV; = ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{0}^{2}∫_{0}^{4 − x − y}dzdydx; = ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{0}^{2}[z]_{z = 0}^{z = 4 − x − y}dydx; = ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{0}^{2}(4 − x − y) − 0dydx; = ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{0}^{2}4 − x − ydydx; = ∫_{0}^{1}[(4 − x)y − (y^{2})/(2)]_{y = 0}^{y = 2}dx; = ∫_{0}^{1}((4 − x)(2) − (2^{2})/(2)) − 0dx; = ∫_{0}^{1}6 − 2xdx; = [6x − x^{2}]_{x = 0}^{x = 1}; = (6(1) − 1^{2}) − 0; = 5]
